subject: Biology
title: Characteristics of Living Things
content:
All living things (organisms) share these features — remember MR NIGER D:
M — Movement
R — Respiration (release energy from food)
N — Nutrition (obtaining food)
I — Irritability/Sensitivity (responding to stimuli)
G — Growth (permanent increase in size)
E — Excretion (removing waste)
R — Reproduction (producing offspring)
D — Death (all living things die)

Living vs non-living: a car moves and uses fuel (energy) but can't grow, reproduce or excrete — so it's not alive.
keyPoints: MR NIGER D covers all 7–8 characteristics
Growth is a permanent increase; a swelling crystal isn't growth
Irritability = response to stimuli like light, touch, gravity

subject: Biology
title: Cell Structure and Functions
content:
The cell is the basic unit of life. Cells are microscopic — discovered by Robert Hooke (1665) in cork.

Plant cell vs animal cell — both have: nucleus (control centre, holds DNA), cytoplasm (jelly where reactions happen), cell membrane (controls what enters/leaves), mitochondria (release energy), ribosomes (protein making).
Plant cells ONLY: cellulose cell wall (rigid support), chloroplasts (photosynthesis, contain chlorophyll), large permanent vacuole (stores water/salts).
keyPoints: Nucleus = control centre with chromosomes
Cell membrane: partially permeable, controls entry/exit
Chloroplasts + cell wall + vacuole = plant-only features

subject: Biology
title: Microscopy and Cell Observation
content:
The microscope magnifies tiny objects. Light microscope: up to ×2000, uses light + glass lenses. Parts: eyepiece, objective lenses (×10 low power, ×40 high power), stage, clips, diaphragm, mirror/light, coarse & fine focus knobs.

Total magnification = eyepiece lens × objective lens. E.g. ×10 eyepiece × ×40 objective = ×400.

Making a slide: thin specimen → drop of water → stain (iodine for starch, methylene blue for onion cells) → coverslip at an angle to avoid air bubbles.
keyPoints: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
Stains: iodine (starch/cell nuclei), methylene blue
Always start focusing with coarse knob at low power

subject: Biology
title: Levels of Organisation in Living Things
content:
Cell → Tissue → Organ → System → Organism.
• Cell: one unit (muscle cell)
• Tissue: similar cells doing one job (muscle tissue)
• Organ: different tissues working together (heart)
• System: organs cooperating (circulatory system)
• Organism: all systems together (you!)

Examples: blood = tissue; leaf, kidney, lung = organs; digestive system = system.
keyPoints: Cell → tissue → organ → system → organism
Heart, lungs, leaf, kidney = organs
Blood is a tissue, not an organ

subject: Biology
title: Nutrition in Plants
content:
Plants are autotrophs — they make their own food by photosynthesis.

Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy (chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

Raw materials: carbon dioxide (through stomata), water (roots, xylem). Conditions: sunlight and chlorophyll.

Experiment to show starch is made in light: destarch a leaf in darkness 24–48 h → cover part of leaf with foil → sunlight several hours → boil in water → ethanol (removes chlorophyll) → iodine. Only the uncovered part turns blue-black = starch made only in light.
keyPoints: Photosynthesis needs CO₂ + H₂O + light + chlorophyll
By-product: oxygen (from photolysis of water)
Starch test: iodine turns blue-black in light-exposed parts

subject: Biology
title: Photosynthesis — Deep Dive
content:
Two stages:
1. Light reaction (grana/thylakoids): chlorophyll captures light, splits water into H + O (photolysis), makes ATP. Oxygen released.
2. Dark reaction / Calvin cycle (stroma): CO₂ combines with hydrogen to build glucose — light not directly needed.

Rate factors: light intensity, CO₂ concentration, temperature, water. Up to a point, increasing each factor increases the rate.

Importance: food + oxygen for all life; removes CO₂ (reduces global warming).
keyPoints: Light reaction: splits water, releases O₂
Dark reaction: fixes CO₂ into glucose
Limiting factors: light, CO₂, temperature

subject: Biology
title: Respiration in Plants and Animals
content:
Respiration = releasing energy from food. Every living cell respires 24/7.

Aerobic: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy (38 ATP) — in mitochondria.
Anaerobic (without oxygen): muscles → lactic acid (causes cramp!); yeast → ethanol + CO₂ (fermentation — brewing & baking).

Compare with photosynthesis: respiration breaks glucose down day & night; photosynthesis builds glucose only in light. In bright light plants photosynthesise faster than they respire, so net gas exchange = O₂ out.
keyPoints: Aerobic: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + 38 ATP
Anaerobic in muscle = lactic acid → fatigue
Fermentation = yeast anaerobic respiration → ethanol

subject: Biology
title: Transport System in Plants
content:
Two transport tissues:
• Xylem — carries water + mineral salts from roots UP to leaves (transpiration stream). Dead hollow cells, no end walls.
• Phloem — carries made food (sucrose, amino acids) both directions = translocation. Living cells.

Transpiration: water evaporates from stomata, pulling the column up (cohesion-tension). Faster with: heat, wind, low humidity. Slower at night (stomata close).

Experiment: celery stick in coloured water shows xylem vessels dyed within hours.
keyPoints: Xylem: water up, one direction, dead cells
Phloem: food translocation, both directions, living cells
Transpiration pull drives water up; stomata control it

subject: Biology
title: Transport System in Animals
content:
The circulatory system: heart (pump) + blood vessels + blood.

Double circulation: pulmonary (heart → lungs → heart, CO₂ out O₂ in) + systemic (heart → body → heart, O₂ out CO₂ in). Blood passes the heart twice per full cycle.

Vessels: arteries (thick, muscular, carry blood AWAY at high pressure), veins (thin, valves, carry blood BACK at low pressure), capillaries (one cell thick — exchange site).

Blood components: plasma (55%, transports), red cells (haemoglobin → oxygen), white cells (defence), platelets (clotting).
keyPoints: Double circulation: pulmonary + systemic
Arteries away, veins back, capillaries exchange
Red cells carry oxygen as oxyhaemoglobin
